A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research lineage, retaining the authors and central dynamical EMA derivation despite the changed title and expanded scope. All 24 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, figures, equations and rotated tables, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaCA experiments on six VQA datasets, including accuracy, forgetting, ablations, zero-shot evaluations and dialogue examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for the revised method across multiple multimodal model configurations, eight multimodal tasks and the 19-task InstrDialog benchmark, plus ablations and instruction-matching results.

M1.justification: v1 continually updates one LoRA/projector parameter set. v2 adds TF-IDF instruction encoding, cosine-similarity grouping, a codebook and parameter pool, conditional parameter reuse or expansion, and instruction-based selection at inference (Section 4.4). It also adapts the procedure to T5 adapters and revises the implemented EMA approximation in Appendix E.

E1.justification: The main continual evaluation expands from six VQA datasets to eight tasks: ImageNet becomes a trained classification task rather than only a held-out zero-shot evaluation, and visual grounding is added. Appendix M adds 19 language-only dialogue tasks. The earlier quantitative evaluation on successive unseen VQA/ImageNet datasets is removed, although qualitative zero-shot dialogue cases remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds EProj, Model Tailor (MT) and Multi-Task to the LLaVA-7B comparison, removes v1's separate full-fine-tuning and Upper-Bond entries, and no longer reports the baseline panel for the ten-template setting. The new InstrDialog comparison includes FT variants, L2, AGEM, replay and AdapterCL (Table 8).

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaVA-13B, Qwen-VL and T5-small configurations. The robustness protocol changes from four combined order/instruction settings to separate comparisons of three task orders and three instruction regimes. Final task accuracy replaces ADA/ADF in the headline plots, and the new NLP evaluation uses ROUGE-L and forward/backward transfer. These changes preclude treating the main version-to-version scores as equivalent-setting comparisons.

E4.justification: v2 adds an incremental instruction-grouping ablation and matching-accuracy analysis, revises order/instruction robustness tests, and replaces the main qualitative examples. v1's quantitative zero-shot-collapse analysis and EMA-weight trajectory plots disappear. The fixed-weight sensitivity experiment is retained with expanded reporting in Appendix F; the four appendix dialogue cases are retained and reordered.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without uncertainty information. v2 Table 8 introduces means and standard deviations for InstrDialog, including the proposed method. Neither version states run counts or seeds, and v2's main multimodal tables still report point estimates.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 reports 61.89 Avg.ACC and 2.68 forgetting for LLaCA; v2 Table 1 reports 64.64 and 1.93 for the revised method on eight tasks. These are replaced results under different conditions, not demonstrated same-setting gains. v2 adds other-backbone, NLP, ablation and matching results, including InstrDialog AR of 39.8 with SD 0.5, while removing earlier zero-shot, runtime and intermediate learning-score tables.

T1.justification: The ideal-state proposition, Taylor/Lagrange derivation and supporting EMA proofs are largely retained under renumbering. However, v2 Appendix E, Eq. 45 adds an approximation of the form ||1-X|| approximately equal to 1-||X||; v1 Appendix A.6, Eq. 58 stops at ||1-X||. This changes the mathematical approximation used for implementation.

C1.justification: v1 presents a multimodal, nonexpanding LLaCA method and emphasizes zero-shot preservation with few additional costs. v2 presents a general continual-instruction framework for language and multimodal models, makes instruction grouping and limited expansion central contributions, and drops the headline emphasis on zero-shot preservation. The contribution's scope and resource-efficiency claim are substantially redefined.

C2.justification: The efficiency rationale changes from maintaining one parameter set to grouping instructions and using inexpensive TF-IDF routing. v2 adds interpretations of positive NLP backward transfer and task-order effects, while removing the quantitative zero-shot-collapse interpretation. The stated applicability limitation shifts from instruction tuning versus future continual pre-training to image/text coverage versus future additional modalities and scenarios.

D1.justification: v2 supplies complete instruction-template and grouping tables, identifies sklearn's TfidfVectorizer, and provides codebook/pool pseudocode and adapter-use details. It newly states the Truth Alignment evaluation criterion without establishing a change from v1. Hardware changes from eight A100s to eight H100s, while the main LoRA hyperparameters remain unchanged. Runtime reporting is removed, the grouping threshold is unspecified, and both PDFs only promise future code release.

R1.justification: Although the bibliography is largely retained, v2 explicitly credits L2P and EProj as inspiration for grouping and adds substantial comparisons with their selection mechanisms in Appendix G. Its positioning shifts from avoiding model expansion to distinguishing lightweight, limited expansion through TF-IDF routing, stored instructions and no learned routing keys.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and terminology, substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, method overview and experimental narrative, moves the task definition into Preliminary, and reorganizes the appendices from A.1–A.11 into A–P. Much mathematical prose survives, but the overall narrative is extensively restructured. Several new citation locations display unresolved question marks.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the headline radars, redraws the workflow around instruction grouping, adds an instruction-reuse illustration, expands the benchmark tables and introduces large instruction/grouping tables. The fixed-EMA bar chart becomes an expanded appendix table, and the EMA trajectory plot series is removed. Existing dialogue figures are reordered and relabeled.

improvement.justification: v1's broad applicability claim was tested only on LLaVA-7B with VQA training. v2 substantially strengthens its support through additional model configurations, language-only tasks, relevant EProj/MT comparisons, and direct grouping ablation and matching tests. Full instruction templates and NLP uncertainty reporting also improve transparency. These gains outweigh the removed quantitative zero-shot and runtime analyses, although efficiency evidence is weaker and the unspecified grouping threshold and unresolved citations limit reproducibility.
